expectations.text: The component implements _getFocused() returning the currently focused poster child (Lightning's real focus delegation mechanism)
expectations.evidence: PosterRow.js does NOT implement _getFocused() at all â€” confirmed by full read of the file (no occurrence of `_getFocused` anywhere in outputs/PosterRow.js). The transcript (section 4) and response.md explicitly document a deliberate design decision NOT to delegate focus to per-poster children: 'keep PosterRow itself as the focus leaf (no _getFocused() override delegating to a child), track _selectedIndex on the row, and have the row directly patch the currently-selected tile's visual state.' The stated rationale is that the poster tiles in this specific input file are plain template-object children (rect/Image/Title, no `type:` pointing at a Component subclass) rather than Lightning.Component instances, so Lightning would not invoke _focus()/_unfocus() lifecycle hooks on them even if _getFocused() returned one â€” making literal child delegation a no-op rather than a working mechanism. Instead, PosterRow implements a full, coherent row-level focus/navigation model: _focus()/_unfocus() (fired when the row itself enters/leaves the focus path), _handleLeft/_handleRight (bounds-checked _selectedIndex updates), and _handleEnter (real action). response.md also explicitly documents the expected integration contract for a parent: `_getFocused() { return this.tag('PosterRow'); }`, i.e. this component is designed to BE the child that a parent delegates to via real _getFocused() delegation, just not itself delegating further down to non-Component tiles. Per the grading instructions' explicit guidance for this expectation, this is judged as a legitimate alternative pattern rather than an automatic fail, because the row does correctly serve as a real, working focus target with a complete navigation model (index tracking, bounds checks, visual feedback, Enter action) â€” there is no case where the app would be left without working navigation. PASS is given on that basis, but graders/skill-authors should note the literal expectation text (child delegation via _getFocused()) was NOT satisfied â€” see eval_feedback.

notes: modal-signal-handler-bug is the only strongly discriminating eval here: with_skill 5/5 vs without_skill 0/5. Without the skill, the model confidently inverted Lightning's own dispatch rule -- it believes signal() looks up a $<name> method directly and that $-prefixed names are the signal() convention, when $-prefixed names actually belong to fireAncestors(). That wrong model led it to treat the pre-existing (actually-dead) $modalClosed() as the working handler and to propose a fix that would not have solved the user's reported bug. The skill's references/communication.md states the real contract plainly, and the with-skill run quoted it almost verbatim to reach the correct root cause (a missing `signals` map).

poster-row-focus-navigation and button-js-to-ts-template-spec scored 5/5 in BOTH configurations, so as written they don't discriminate skill-present vs skill-absent behavior for this model -- it already produces idiomatic Lightning v2 focus-handling and TemplateSpec typing from general training knowledge. That's a useful finding in itself (this model needs the skill least for 'default-path' tasks it already knows well), but it means these two evals mostly stress-test whether the skill's guidance *matches* already-good defaults rather than whether it *changes* behavior. Consider evolving them toward less mainstream corners of Lightning v2 (e.g. nested _states(), passSignals forwarding, texture/performance tradeoffs) where a baseline model is more likely to guess wrong.

The poster-row-focus-navigation with_skill run reported 54277 tokens versus its without_skill counterpart's 5574 and the other evals' 4500-6000 range -- a ~10x outlier. This looks like a data-capture artifact (that run's grading.json had a null self-reported timing/token field, so the aggregator fell back to the executor's whole-task total_tokens from the task notification, which is a different and larger unit than the output_chars proxy used elsewhere) rather than a genuine 10x cost difference. Treat the with_skill token mean (21930, stddev 28014) as unreliable until token accounting is made consistent across runs; don't read the current with_skill/without_skill token delta at face value.

Grader feedback (not a hard failure) on two poster-row expectations: 'implements _getFocused() returning the currently focused poster child' assumes per-child Component delegation as the only valid pattern, but a legitimate alternative -- keeping the row itself as the focus leaf and manually tracking a selected index -- also produces working navigation and shows up in both configurations' outputs. Consider loosening this assertion's wording (or adding a second acceptable-pattern clause) before reusing it in iteration 2, and separately, the skill's own focus-and-input.md apparently states a rail/list component should 'always include the _getFocused() override' without carving out this row-as-leaf exception -- worth checking that reference file's wording during the next skill revision.
